title_en: Opinion of the Supreme People's Court on Further Strengthening the Concept of Good Faith and Civilized Enforcement in Enforcement Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Further Strengthening the Concept of Good-Faith and Civilized Enforcement in Enforcement Work

Fa Fa [2019] No. 35

In order to implement the spirit of documents such as the "Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Improving the Property Rights Protection System and Legally Protecting Property Rights" and the "Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Creating a Better Development Environment to Support the Reform and Development of Private Enterprises," to further enhance the level of strict, standardized, fair, and civilized enforcement by the People's Courts, to promote the sustained, healthy, and high-level operation of enforcement work, and to provide higher quality judicial services and guarantees for economic and social development, the following opinions are proposed in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual circumstances of the People's Courts' enforcement work.

I. Fully Recognize the Important Significance and Essential Spirit of Good-Faith and Civilized Enforcement

1. Fully recognize the important significance of good-faith and civilized enforcement. Enforcement is the final link in the last line of defense for fairness and justice. Strengthening the concept of good-faith and civilized enforcement, while legally protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the winning party, minimizing the impact on the rights and interests of the person subject to enforcement, and achieving an organic unity of legal and social effects, is an inevitable requirement for maintaining social fairness and justice and promoting social harmony and stability. It is an inherent meaning of improving the property rights protection system, establishing and perfecting a market-oriented, rule-of-law-based, and internationalized business environment, and promoting high-quality development. It is of great significance for comprehensively advancing the rule of law and modernizing the national governance system and governance capacity.

2. Accurately grasp the essential spirit of good-faith and civilized enforcement. Enforcement work is an important means of realizing judgments in favor of the prevailing party by relying on the compulsory force of the state. At present, evasion of enforcement and avoidance of enforcement by persons subject to enforcement remain the main contradictions and prominent issues in enforcement work. Emphasizing the compulsory nature of enforcement, continuously increasing enforcement efforts, and timely ensuring that the winning party realizes its legitimate rights and interests remain the focus and main line of enforcement work. However, at the same time, attention must be paid to the significant impact of enforcement work on all parties involved. During the enforcement process, the People's Courts must also strengthen the concept of good-faith and civilized enforcement, strictly and normatively guarantee the legitimate rights and interests of all parties; adhere to the principle of proportionality, find the balance point of interests between the two parties, and avoid excessive enforcement; raise political standing, focus on the overall strategy of the Party and national development, and improve the ability and level of grasping judicial policies, achieving the unity of performing duties according to law and serving the overall situation and promoting development. Effective measures should be taken to resolutely correct the phenomena of excessive seizure and disorderly seizure that appear in practice, smooth the channels for the masses to report problems, implement "double investigation of a case" for relevant clues, and legally and seriously deal with non-standard behaviors.

In the process of strengthening the concept of good-faith and civilized enforcement, the People's Courts must fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of creditors, maintain enforcement authority and judicial credibility, and focus coercive power on legally cracking down on and punishing acts of evasion, avoidance, and resistance to enforcement. They must resolutely prevent enforcement personnel from passively enforcing or delaying enforcement under the pretext of "good-faith and civilized enforcement," or from unprincipledly facilitating reconciliation between the two parties under the pretext of reducing the impact on the person subject to enforcement, thereby harming the legitimate rights and interests of creditors.

II. Strictly Prohibit Excessive Seizure and Disorderly Seizure

3. Reasonably select enforcement property. Where the person subject to enforcement has multiple properties available for enforcement, the People's Court shall select property that has a relatively small impact on the production and life of the person subject to enforcement and is convenient for enforcement. Without affecting the efficiency and effectiveness of enforcement, if the person subject to enforcement requests the People's Court to enforce a certain piece of property first, such request shall be granted; if not granted, there must be reasonable and正当 reasons.

During the enforcement process, the People's Court shall reserve necessary living expenses for the person subject to enforcement and their dependents. It must strictly follow the central government's spirit on property rights protection, strictly distinguish between enterprise legal person property and shareholder personal property, strictly prohibit illegally seizing property of persons not involved in the case, and strictly prohibit taking enforcement measures on property that cannot be seized, effectively protecting the legitimate rights and interests of private enterprises and other enterprise legal persons, entrepreneurs, and various market entities. Note that trust property is independent of the respective固有财产 of the trustor and trustee during the trust duration, and the beneficiary's rights to trust property are manifested as trust beneficiary rights; trust property is not the beneficiary's liability property. Therefore, if a party applies for preservation or enforcement measures against trust funds in the special accounts of depositary banks or trust companies due to disputes with the trustor, trustee, or beneficiary, except in circumstances specified in Article 17 of the Trust Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall not grant such application.

4. Strictly prohibit excessive seizure. Compulsory enforcement of the person subject to enforcement's property shall be limited to the amount of the value sufficient to satisfy the debt determined by the effective legal instrument, and clearly excessive seizure must be resolutely prohibited. Where freezing deposits in the bank account of the person subject to enforcement, the specific frozen amount shall be clearly specified, and the circulation of funds and use of the account beyond the frozen amount shall not be affected. Where the overall value of the immovable property to be seized is clearly excessive relative to the debt amount, seizure measures shall be taken against the corresponding value portion of the immovable property; if the relevant department claims that it cannot handle separate seizures because the immovable property is registered under the same certificate of title, after the People's Court has conducted an overall seizure of the immovable property, upon application by the person subject to enforcement, it shall promptly coordinate with the relevant department to handle separate registration and lift the seizure on the excessive portion. If the relevant department, without正当 reasons, refuses to assist in handling separate registration and seizure, corresponding penalty measures shall be taken in accordance with Article 114 of the Civil Procedure Law.

5. Flexibly adopt seizure measures. For property that can be "live-seized," try not to conduct "dead-seizure," so that the seized property can be put to its best use and avoid waste of social resources. Where seizing production materials such as factory buildings and machinery equipment of the person subject to enforcement, if continued use by the person subject to enforcement has no significant impact on the value of the property, such use may be permitted. For real estate development enterprises experiencing capital turnover difficulties and temporarily unable to repay debts, the People's Court shall handle the case according to the following circumstances:

(1) After seizing a construction in progress, in principle, the person subject to enforcement shall be allowed to continue construction.

(2) After seizing a construction in progress, if compulsory realization measures against it can realize the creditor's rights of the enforcement creditor but will clearly diminish the property's value and be manifestly unfair to the person subject to enforcement, the court shall actively facilitate a settlement agreement between the parties to suspend enforcement, and realize the property after the construction is completed; if no settlement agreement can be reached, but the person subject to enforcement provides corresponding security and promises to complete the construction within a reasonable period, the compulsory realization measures may be suspended.

(3) After seizing commercial housing under construction or existing housing, under the premise of ensuring control over the corresponding proceeds, the court may supervise the person subject to enforcement to sell the houses by itself at a reasonable price within a certain period. When determining the period, the People's Court shall specify clear time nodes to avoid excessively long periods affecting enforcement efficiency and harming the legitimate rights and interests of the enforcement creditor.

6. Fully leverage the financing function of seized property. After the People's Court seizes property, if the person subject to preservation or the person subject to enforcement applies to use the seized property for financing, the matter shall be handled according to the following circumstances:

(1) After seizing property for preservation, if the person subject to preservation applies to use the seized property for financing to replace the seized property, under the premise of ensuring control over the corresponding financing funds, the court may supervise the person subject to preservation to conduct financing at a reasonable price.

(2) During the enforcement process, if the person subject to enforcement applies to use the seized property for financing to repay debts, with the consent of the enforcement creditor or if the financing funds are sufficient to repay all enforcement debts, such application may be granted.

If the person subject to preservation or the person subject to enforcement uses the seized property for financing, and the lender requires that the property mortgage or pledge registration be completed before releasing funds, the People's Court shall actively coordinate with relevant departments to handle matters such as property unsealing, mortgage or pledge registration, and strictly control the financing funds.

7. Strictly regulate the freezing of listed company stocks. In order to maintain the stability of the capital market, legally protect the legitimate rights and interests of creditors and the investment rights of debtors, when the People's Court freezes the stocks of a debtor in a listed company, it shall strictly implement the following provisions:

(1) Strictly prohibit excessive freezing. Freezing of listed company stocks shall be limited to the amount of value sufficient to satisfy the debt determined by the effective legal instrument. Stock value shall be determined based on the closing price on the trading day before freezing, combined with the stock market conditions, generally within a range of no more than 20%. After the freeze, if the value undergoes significant changes, upon application by the party, the People's Court may add additional freezes or lift part of the freeze.

(2) Freeze with sellability. After freezing stocks for preservation, if the person subject to preservation applies to change the freeze measure to a freeze with sellability, it shall be granted, provided that the funds account of the person subject to preservation at the securities company is frozen in advance within a clearly specified amount. During the enforcement process, if the person subject to enforcement applies to sell stocks by itself through secondary market trading to repay debts, the People's Court may handle it in accordance with the aforementioned provisions, but shall require that the sale be completed within 10 trading days. Under special circumstances, the period may be appropriately extended.

(3) Freezing of pledged stocks. If the listed company stocks are subject to a pledge and the pledgee is not the preservation applicant or enforcement applicant in this case, currently, when the People's Court takes freezing measures, because it is necessary to include the existing pledge claims on the stocks and such claim amounts are often difficult to calculate accurately, especially when there are multiple pledges on the stocks, it is also necessary to specify which pledged stocks are to be frozen. To protect the legitimate rights and interests of ordinary creditors, the People's Court generally freezes all pledged stocks. This carries the risk of excessive freezing and also affects the pledgee's ability to realize its claims by itself, and is not in line with the principle of enforcement economy.

After communication and coordination between the Supreme People's Court and the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited (hereinafter "CSDC") will modify the existing freezing system, establishing a new method for freezing pledged stocks, which will be formally implemented after the system modification is completed. The specific contents are as follows:

First, if the stocks held by the debtor in a listed company are subject to a pledge and the pledgee is not the preservation applicant or enforcement applicant in this case, when the People's Court freezes the pledged stocks, it shall freeze the corresponding quantity of stocks according to the calculation method specified in 7(1), without including the amount of the pledge claim. When freezing pledged stocks, the People's Court shall first freeze the debtor's funds account at the securities company, and specify a clear freeze amount, and shall not freeze the entire funds account.

Second, after the freeze, it does not affect the pledgee's ability to realize its claims by liquidating the stocks. If the pledgee releases any portion of the pledged stocks, the freeze effect automatically applies to the released portion within the scope of the frozen stock quantity. If there is a surplus after the pledgee realizes its claims by liquidating the stocks, the freeze effect automatically applies to the remaining proceeds within the amount of the claims in this case.

Third, during the enforcement process, to realize the claims in this case, the People's Court may take compulsory realization measures against the corresponding quantity of stocks within the amount of the pledge claim and the claim in this case, and shall first satisfy the pledge claim before satisfying the debt in this case.

Fourth, if two or more state organs freeze the same pledged stocks, the freeze order shall be determined according to the time the stock freeze procedures are handled at the securities company or CSDC, satisfying the freeze needs of each state organ in turn. If two or more state organs freeze the same pledged stocks at the securities company and CSDC respectively on the same trading day, the one that handles the stock freeze procedures at the securities company first shall have the prior freeze.

Fifth, if disputes arise between the People's Court and other state organs regarding the freezing of pledged stocks, the Supreme People's Court shall take the initiative to coordinate and resolve the matter with the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and other relevant departments according to law. During the period of dispute coordination and resolution, the securities company or CSDC shall control the stocks subject to the dispute and shall not assist either party in enforcement. After the dispute coordination and resolution is completed, the securities company or CSDC shall handle the matter according to the final conclusion reached through consultation by the disputing organs.

Sixth, the aforementioned provisions do not apply to freezes completed before the system modification is completed. If the preservation applicant or enforcement applicant in the case is the pledgee, the aforementioned provisions on freezing measures do not apply.

III. Legally and Appropriately Adopt Measures for Property Realization

8. Reasonably determine the reference price for property disposal. During the enforcement process, the People's Court shall reasonably determine the reference price for property disposal in accordance with the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Determination of Reference Prices for Property Disposal by People's Courts." Without harming the legitimate rights and interests of third parties, the court shall actively facilitate the parties to reach agreement on the reference price, to further improve the efficiency of determining the reference price and avoid subsequent disputes. If the property has a tax base price, government pricing, or government guidance price, and the parties cannot or do not agree on a negotiated price, or both parties request a directed inquiry, the People's Court shall actively coordinate with relevant agencies to handle the inquiry. If the result of the directed inquiry seriously deviates from the market price, appropriate corrections may be made. Practice has shown that online inquiries are not only efficient but also the vast majority of inquiry results can basically reflect the true market price. For properties that do not require on-site inspection or appraisal by professionals, the People's Court shall actively guide the parties to determine the reference price through online inquiry and review the inquiry report.

If the reference price is determined through entrusted appraisal, and the person subject to enforcement believes that the appraised price seriously deviates from the market price and raises an objection, to improve work efficiency, the People's Court may, based on the appraised price, first facilitate the parties to reach agreement on the reference price. If agreement cannot be reached quickly, the matter shall be submitted to the appraisal agency for a written explanation. If the appraisal agency fails to provide an explanation within the time limit or the person subject to enforcement still has objections, the matter shall be promptly submitted to the relevant industry association for professional technical review. During the process of determining the reference price for property disposal, the People's Court shall perform its supervisory duties according to law, and if it discovers malicious collusion between parties, bidders, and relevant institutions or personnel to lower the reference price, it shall promptly investigate and rectify.

9. Appropriately expand the application scenarios of private sale procedures. On the basis of adhering to the principle of priority for online judicial auction, comprehensively considering the actual situation of the property to be realized, whether it will harm the interests of the enforcement creditor, third party, or social public interest, measures such as direct private sale or compulsory sale may be appropriately adopted.

(1) If the person subject to enforcement applies to sell the seized property by itself to repay the debt, under the premise of ensuring control over the corresponding proceeds, the court may supervise the sale at a reasonable price within a certain period. The sale period shall be determined by the People's Court based on factors such as the actual situation of the property and market conditions, but shall not exceed 60 days.

(2) If the person subject to enforcement applies to directly sell the seized property without going through an auction, with the consent of the enforcement creditor or if the sale proceeds are sufficient to repay all enforcement debts, the People's Court may directly sell without auction.

(3) If the person subject to enforcement believes that the online inquiry or appraised price is too low and applies to sell the seized property by itself at a price no lower than the online inquiry or appraised price to repay the debt, upon review, if the People's Court finds no circumstances of malicious collusion between the person subject to enforcement and others to dispose of the property at a low price, it may supervise the sale within a certain period.

(4) If the property fails to sell at auction and the enforcement creditor does not accept the property in lieu of debt, and a third party applies to purchase at the failed auction price, it may be permitted.

(5) After the second online judicial auction fails, if the person subject to enforcement proposes to raise funds using the failed auction price, the People's Court shall consider the matter in its discretion, taking into account the basic situation of the auctioned property, the degree of difference between the failed auction price and the market price, and the financing period. If financing is permitted, the procedure for property in lieu of debt or compulsory sale shall not be initiated temporarily.

If the person subject to enforcement applies for private sale under 9(3) and is permitted by the People's Court, and subsequently files an objection with the People's Court in accordance with Articles 22 and 23 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Determination of Reference Prices for Property Disposal by People's Courts," such objection shall not be accepted; if the person subject to enforcement files an objection to the online inquiry or appraised price and subsequently applies for private sale under 9(3), such application shall not be granted.

10. Fully attract more entities to participate in bidding. During the auction process, the People's Court shall fully and truthfully disclose the current status, possession and use, ancillary obligations, known defects and rights burdens, bidding qualifications, and other matters of the auctioned property, and shall strictly prohibit deliberately concealing defects to induce bidders to bid, and strictly prohibit deliberately exaggerating defects to mislead bidders to bid. If the auctioned property is immovable and the person subject to enforcement or others have no right to occupy, the People's Court shall be responsible for vacating and delivering the property according to law, and shall not include information such as "not responsible for vacating and delivery" in the public announcement. The professional advantages of online auction platforms and auction auxiliary institutions shall be fully utilized to carry out video promotion of the auction items, targeted push of auction information to professional market entities, on-site inspections, etc., to attract more market entities to participate in bidding.

11. Maximize the realization of the true value of property. If there are a large number of the same type of enforcement property, and the person subject to enforcement believes that batch realization or overall realization can maximize its value, the People's Court may permit it. Especially for large-scale immovable properties such as entire buildings, entire floors of buildings, contiguous shops or villas, if they have been separately registered or can be separately registered afterwards, and the person subject to enforcement believes that batch realization can maximize the value of the immovable property, generally such application shall be granted. When multiple properties are realized separately, if the proceeds from the sale of part of the properties are sufficient to repay the debt, the realization of the remaining properties shall be stopped, unless the person subject to enforcement consents to the sale of all properties.

12. Accurately grasp the method for realizing the usufruct pledge on immovable property. If the effective legal instrument determines that the applying enforcement creditor has a pledge on the usufruct right of the person subject to enforcement to receive income from roads, bridges, tunnels, etc., and the applying enforcement creditor deducts funds from the fee collection account of the usufruct right by itself to realize its pledge claim, and other creditors object to the People's Court on the grounds that the applying enforcement creditor only has a pledge on the fee collection right but not on the funds in the fee collection account, such objection shall not be supported. During the enforcement process, the People's Court may deduct funds from the fee collection account of the usufruct right to realize the pledge claim of the applying enforcement creditor. If the funds in the fee collection account are sufficient to repay the debt, compulsory realization of the usufruct right of the person subject to enforcement shall not be carried out.

IV. Make Full Use of Systems Such as Enforcement Settlement and Bankruptcy Reorganization

13. Legally make good use of relevant systems such as enforcement settlement and bankruptcy reorganization. While legally taking enforcement measures, the enforcement opportunity shall be properly grasped, enforcement strategies shall be carefully planned, and enforcement methods shall be noted. For enterprises with a temporary break in the capital chain but still having development potential and the possibility of rescue, the enterprise's assets may be revitalized through means such as settlement by installment performance, merger and restructuring, or introduction of third-party funds. Efforts to promote the concept of bankruptcy protection shall be intensified, and through explanations and other means, enforcement creditors or persons subject to enforcement shall be guided to agree to legally transfer the case to bankruptcy proceedings. For enterprises with operational value, bankruptcy reorganization and bankruptcy settlement shall be used to resolve debt crises, fully leveraging the rescue function of the bankruptcy system, helping enterprises out of difficulties, balancing the interests of creditors, debtors, investors, employees, and other interested parties, and achieving optimization of resource allocation and maximization of overall social value through the market.

V. Strictly Regulate the Measures of Including in the List of Dishonest Persons and Restricting Consumption

14. Strict application of conditions and procedures. The adoption of measures to include a person in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement or to impose consumption restrictions must strictly comply with the conditions and procedures stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Publication of Information on the List of Dishonest Persons Subject to Enforcement (hereinafter referred to as the Dishonesty List Provisions), and the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning Restricting High Consumption and Related Consumption of Persons Subject to Enforcement. For persons subject to enforcement who do not meet the statutory conditions, measures of inclusion in the dishonesty list or consumption restrictions must resolutely not be taken as disciplinary sanctions. For persons subject to enforcement who meet the statutory conditions, where a decision to adopt disciplinary measures is made, a written decision or consumption restriction order shall be prepared and, in accordance with the law, signed and issued after review by the president of the court.

It must be particularly noted that, according to the provisions of judicial interpretations, although a decision to include a person in the dishonesty list takes effect upon being signed and issued by the president of the court, it shall be served on the parties in accordance with the service methods stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law. Phenomena that do not comply with statutory procedures, such as signing and issuing without serving, must be resolutely eliminated.

15. Appropriate grace period setting. Depending on the specific circumstances of the case, courts at various levels may grant a grace period of one to three months to persons subject to enforcement who are decided to be included in the dishonesty list or subjected to consumption restriction measures. During the grace period, their information on dishonesty or consumption restrictions shall be temporarily not released. Upon expiration of the grace period, if the person subject to enforcement still fails to perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument, their information shall then be released and corresponding disciplinary measures shall be taken.

16. Several types of circumstances where disciplinary measures are not to be taken. Where a person subject to enforcement has the ability to perform but refuses to perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument, or refuses to perform a settlement agreement without justifiable reasons, but the people's court has already controlled sufficient property of such person to satisfy the debt, or the applying for execution party requests that disciplinary measures be temporarily not taken, then the person subject to enforcement shall not be subjected to measures of inclusion in the dishonesty list or consumption restrictions. Where the entity is a dishonest person subject to enforcement, the people's court shall not include its legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible persons affecting debt performance, actual controller, or other such persons in the dishonesty list. Where a full-time student becomes a person subject to enforcement due to a "campus loan" dispute, such student generally shall not be subjected to measures of inclusion in the dishonesty list or consumption restrictions.

17. Several types of circumstances for lifting consumption restriction measures. After the people's court has taken consumption restriction measures against a person subject to enforcement, if the person subject to enforcement or their relevant persons apply for the lifting or temporary lifting of such measures, the following circumstances shall be handled separately:

(1) After an entity person subject to enforcement has been subjected to consumption restrictions, if its legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible persons affecting debt performance, or actual controller submits a request, on the grounds of personal consumption, to engage in consumption activities using personal property, and upon review it is verified to be true, such request shall be permitted.

(2) After an entity person subject to enforcement has been subjected to consumption restrictions, if its legal representative or principal responsible person genuinely needs to be changed due to operational management requirements, and the former legal representative or principal responsible person applies for the lifting of consumption restriction measures against themselves, they shall provide evidence proving that they are not the actual controller or directly responsible person affecting debt performance of the entity. If, upon review, the people's court verifies this to be true, the application shall be granted, and consumption restriction measures shall be taken against the changed legal representative or principal responsible person in accordance with the law.

(3) Where an individual subjected to consumption restrictions needs to travel to another locality due to emergency circumstances such as seeking medical treatment for a major illness of themselves or their close relatives, funeral arrangements for close relatives, or execution or assistance in execution of official duties, participation in foreign affairs activities or important examinations, and applies to the people's court for temporary lifting of the restrictions on taking airplanes and high-speed rail, upon strict review and with the approval of the president of the court, a temporary lifting period not exceeding one month may be granted.

When the above-mentioned persons submit an application to the people's court, they shall provide sufficient and valid evidence and make a written commitment as required. If false evidence is provided or consumption activities are conducted in breach of the commitment, the people's court shall promptly reinstate the consumption restriction measures against them, simultaneously impose heavier penalties in accordance with Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law, and shall not approve any subsequent application.

18. Smoothing relief channels for disciplinary measures. Where a natural person, legal person, or other organization applies for correction of their inclusion in the dishonesty list, the people's court shall promptly review and make a decision in accordance with the procedures and time limits stipulated in Article 12 of the Dishonesty List Provisions. For applications for correction of consumption restriction measures, the provisions of Article 12 of the Dishonesty List Provisions shall be applied by reference.

If a people's court discovers that there may be errors in the inclusion of a person in the dishonesty list or the imposition of consumption restriction measures, it shall promptly conduct a self-examination and take corresponding action. If a higher-level court discovers errors in a lower-level court's inclusion of a person in the dishonesty list or imposition of consumption restriction measures, it shall order the lower court to promptly correct them, or it may directly correct them in accordance with the law.

19. Timely deletion of dishonest information. Where information on the dishonesty list should be deleted (or blocked) in accordance with the law, timely measures for deletion (or blocking) shall be taken. If deletion (or blocking) measures are taken after more than three working days, or if measures could have been taken immediately but were not taken within three working days, resulting in serious consequences, the responsible persons shall be held accountable in accordance with the law.

If a person subject to enforcement is included simultaneously in a fixed-term dishonesty list and a non-fixed-term dishonesty list due to multiple types of dishonest conduct, after such person has voluntarily performed all obligations determined by the effective legal instrument, generally the information on both the fixed-term list and the non-fixed-term list shall be deleted (or blocked) simultaneously.

20. Accurately understanding the restriction on the enrollment of children of persons subject to enforcement in high-tuition schools. The restriction on the enrollment of children of persons subject to enforcement in high-tuition schools means restricting their children from attending schools with fees exceeding the normal charging standard. Even if the school is a private school, if its fees do not exceed the normal standard, it is not within the scope of the restriction. When taking this measure, the people's court shall strictly review it in accordance with the law and shall not affect the right of the children of persons subject to enforcement to receive normal education. When the news media misreport or misinterpret the people's court's adoption of this measure, the court shall promptly respond and clarify. Where the people's court, after review in accordance with the law, decides to restrict the enrollment of a child of a person subject to enforcement in a high-tuition school, it shall properly communicate with the child and the school to avoid adverse impacts on the child as much as possible.

21. Exploring the establishment of a disciplinary classification and grading mechanism and a credit incentive mechanism. Courts at various levels, in light of their actual work, may actively explore taking graded and classified measures of dishonesty disciplinary sanctions and consumption restrictions against persons subject to enforcement based on the specific circumstances of the case, so that such measures are more precise and more in line with the principle of proportionality.

While carrying out dishonesty disciplinary sanctions in accordance with the law, courts at various levels, in light of their actual work, may explore the implementation of credit incentive measures such as issuing certificates of automatic performance of effective legal instruments, pushing automatic performance information to credit reference agencies, and appropriately reducing the amount of litigation preservation guarantees for honest debtors in accordance with the law, thereby creating a favorable atmosphere that encourages automatic performance and supports honesty and trustworthiness.

VI. Increasing efforts in the distribution of case funds

22. Comprehensive implementation of the "one case, one account" system. After case funds arrive and there is no dispute, the people's court shall, in accordance with the provisions, promptly return them to the execution creditor within one month. If part of the case funds is in dispute, the undisputed portion shall be promptly distributed first. Currently, the Supreme People's Court is comprehensively implementing the "one case, one account" system. Courts at various levels shall strictly implement the deployment and use of the system in accordance with the prescribed time nodes and standard requirements, ensuring that the receipt and distribution of case funds are open and transparent, timely and efficient, with full traceability, effectively plugging loopholes in fund management, eliminating potential risks to integrity and clean government, and maximizing the protection of the lawful rights and interests of all parties.

December 16, 2019
